about: The queue rules, shared by the web Queue (src/player/queue.ts) and the native queue (NativeQueue, run by QueueRulesTest). Every case starts from `list` with `start` current (list index), shuffle and repeat as given, then runs `steps` in order. Ids are track ids; ids are unique within a case. Ops: setList {ids, start} (a new list: replaces the list and the autoplay tracks, keeps the queued ones); queueNext {ids}; addAuto {ids} (autoplay appends these); skipTo {id, lap} (a tap: the list index of that id; a track further ahead moves to right after the current one first, so what it jumps over stays next; a tap that moves on (on the list on the way), shuffle or not, brings along only the current list's songs it jumped over that weren't heard this lap, and the others it jumped over (heard ones, earlier lists') stay behind it, in Played; shuffled, a tap from a song before the current list to one of it leaves the earlier lists' heard songs it jumps over behind it too; lap: a tap on a 'From the top' row, which enters the next lap, so the heard songs you queued leave, as when the list loops); next (a user skip); nextAuto (the track ended by itself); prev {positionMs} (go back: moves when positionMs <= 3000, else restarts the current track); remove {id, nth} (nth: the nth copy of that id in list order, 0 when absent; if it is the current one, the next one in play order becomes current, else the first one in play order, paused, as Media3's); move {id, to} (Up next's up and down: to where the item at list index `to` is, or at `toId`'s list index, as Up next's rows give it; with shuffle on, a song you queued moved past another one also plays in its new place, as shuffle never mixes them, and the others keep their place in play order; never into another list: unless both are songs you queued, which belong to no list, a move whose two ends sit on different sides of a marker (where the current list starts, where the one on the way does) does nothing, and each marker stays at its place in the list, on the first song from there that you didn't queue); setShuffle {on}; setRepeat {mode}; restore {id, kind, beforeId, beforeIndex, mine, auto, heard, earlier} (Undo of a remove: beforeId is the song that followed it in play order, the one at list index beforeIndex if it has that id (a station's next round repeats ids), else the first with that id; kind played puts id back among the played, right before beforeId among every track before the current one in play order, heard or not, else right before the current track, as a list track (an autoplay track when auto is true), with the queued-by-you mark when mine is true; kind top (a 'From the top' row) puts it back the same way, but not heard; otherwise it puts id back as a queued, list or autoplay track (list: of the list you're in, an autoplay track of it when auto is true; autoplay: of the list on the way; a list track with the queued-by-you mark when mine is true, heard when heard is true), right before the first track after the current one, in play order, that is beforeId (for a queued track only a queued one, for the others never a queued one); with no such track, or beforeId null, at the end of that section: queued after the queued run, list after the last track ahead of its own tag (else after the queued run), autoplay at the very end. A list track never goes at or past the first song on the way, in play order or in list order. With earlier true (it is of an earlier list, before the current list's marker) it goes back before that marker in list order, and with shuffle off in play order too. In list order it goes right before the track that follows it in play order, or at the end; with shuffle on, a queued track goes after the queued run there and a list track before the autoplay tracks of the list you're in, so both stay ahead once shuffle is off. Never at or before the current track. It stays in its own list: the first song of the current list or of the one on the way (an autoplay one), put back right before the song that took its place (the songs you queued between don't count), starts that list again, and with shuffle on so does a played song of the current list put back right before its first song; with shuffle on, an autoplay track put back before one on the way goes where that list starts in list order, and starts it again if it came from it, else it ends the list you're in); removeRow {id, from} (✕ on that row of Up next, or of Played or 'From the top' when from is 'played' or 'top': it goes, and its Undo is kept as the page's undoOf keeps it from what the player publishes: the row's own kind (a suggestion of the list you're in, before what's on the way, as kind list with auto; a 'From the top' song you heard as played), the song after it in play order, heard or not, and its list index once this one is gone (or null), its queued-by-you mark, autoplay tag and heard state, and whether it is of an earlier list); undo (restore with what removeRow kept); removeIds {ids} (every item with one of these ids goes; if the current one goes, the next one in play order that stays becomes current, else the first one in play order (paused: Media3 lands there, ended), else nothing plays); dropOnTheWay (autoplay turned off: the list on the way goes, except the songs queued by you); keepTop (keeps the next lap, what 'From the top' shows: the play order from its first song to the current one, without the songs you queued). An expect step checks: current (id); listStart (the id where the current list starts in list order: its marker's song, or the first song when unset); played (the play order before the current track, oldest first); upNext (the whole play order after the current track); upNextStartsWith (its first ids, for shuffled cases); queued (how many leading upNext tracks are 'Queued by you'); list (list order); Up next's three sections, each row by its own kind, never by its place (as the native player sends the kinds): queuedIds (queued by you), listIds (the rest of the list, in play order), listSet (the same ids in any order, for shuffled cases), autoplayIds (autoplay, in play order), autoplaySet (the same ids in any order, for shuffled cases); mine (the ids carrying the 'queued by you' mark, in list order: every song you queued keeps it after it plays, except the one that starts playing because nothing was); upNextIsKeptTop (the current track and then Up next are exactly what keepTop kept); top (the next lap, what 'From the top' shows: with Repeat all only, the play order from its first song up to the one before the current track, without the songs you queued); topSet (the same ids in any order, for shuffled cases); and place (Now Playing's 'N of M', the page's placeOf: the web runner only. N is the playing song's place in the current list and M its songs, the songs you queued not counted; a song you queued has no place (''); after Previous into the list before, the place in the list you started, also its songs that came along into the current one); and heardMine (Save's memory, as [id, after] pairs: each song you queued that played since the list started, in the order it first played, with the id of the song current before it).
rule: Played is what was heard before the current track: the tracks of this list before it in play order that have been current, never the ones before where a list started or a shuffle put them. Queued tracks play right after the current track, first in first out (or as moved with up and down), shuffle or not, until each one plays or is removed. A manual jump (skipTo, or prev moving back) keeps the still-queued tracks next: they move to just after the new current track, in the order they were going to play. Jumping to a queued track plays it; the others stay next. A new list replaces the list and the autoplay tracks, but the queued tracks stay next, in order. Autoplay tracks play after the list in the order added: they are the list on the way, and moving on to one of them (played on to, or tapped) makes the current list start at it or at the first of them, whichever comes first in list order, so with shuffle on the ones before it in the batch stay ahead; a tap that moves on, shuffle or not, brings the current list's songs it jumped over that weren't heard this lap into the new list, at its start, and the heard ones it jumped over (Previous walked back over them) stay behind it, in Played, as do an earlier list's; shuffled, so do the earlier lists' heard songs a tap from one of them (Previous took you there) to one of the current list jumps over (the unheard ones stay ahead). Shuffle mixes what hasn't played of the current list, afresh each time it is turned on: what Played shows stays behind, in the order it played, and so do the songs of earlier lists (before the current list's marker); ahead, the queued tracks come first, then the songs you walked back over (heard, still ahead: Previous or a tap back), in the order you heard them, then the current list's other songs (also those before where it started) mixed, then the list on the way, mixed on its own. Once Repeat all starts the list over, the lap ahead is all still to come: it is mixed (or back in list order), heard last lap or not; only what you heard in this lap counts as walked back over. New autoplay tracks then go at the end, mixed among themselves. Shuffle off keeps the same parts and puts the mixed ones back in list order: Played as heard, the playing track, the queued ones, the songs walked back over, the current list's unheard songs in list order, then what's on the way; a heard song never comes ahead again and an unheard one is never skipped. The list then takes that order: unshuffled, list order is play order (what Save saves), and the current list starts at its first song in it that you didn't queue. Repeat all loops the list you're in: turning it on drops the suggestions on the way and the songs before the current list, heard or not, keeping the playing song and the queued ones; a radio's first suggestions are its list, so they stay. The song playing when it is turned on, if it is before the current list and not one you queued (Previous took you back to it), leaves once another song plays; only that one. A tap from such a song on one of the current list, which moves it right after the playing song, starts the current list at it. Repeat all never brings back a song you queued: when the list loops (a song ending or a Next goes from its last song in play order to its first, Media3's order[0]), or a tap on a 'From the top' row enters the next lap, the heard songs you queued leave the queue, except the one playing; the others keep their order. The loop starts at the first song in play order that stays, never at a heard song you queued. Previous, or a tap on a song you heard, walks back: they stay and play again. Autoplay adds nothing while it is on, and turning autoplay off drops only what is on the way, never the list you're in. Repeat one replays the current track when it ends and leaves Up next as it is; a user skip moves on, as with repeat off (Media3's: none at the end). Jumping to an autoplay track keeps the autoplay tracks after it; more follow them. Up and down never move a song into another list (they stop at the line between the current list and the one on the way, and at where the current list starts); when a list's first song goes, the next song that stays and that you didn't queue starts it. Undo of a removal puts back the same song, as it was, where it was: its own kind and tag (a suggestion stays a suggestion, also from Played), heard or not as it was, with its queued-by-you mark, in its own list (a song of the current list never at or past what's on the way, one of an earlier list never after the current list's marker), right before the song that followed it in play order, heard or not, matched by its place first, as a station's next round repeats ids. Save's memory: the player remembers each song you queued as it first plays, with the song current before it, also after Repeat all takes it out of the queue (the loop, a 'From the top' tap); a new list starts it over; ✕ on a song you queued forgets it, and its Undo remembers it again; removeIds forgets its ids, also of songs no longer in the queue.
